key_insight: RareLens aligns differing reasoning from multiple large language models into one stepwise rare-disease care system, aiming to support screening, diagnosis, treatment planning, and prognosis end to end.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help clinicians navigate rare diseases earlier and more consistently in settings where expertise is scarce and presentations are nonspecific.
method: Four-module pipeline for risk screening, diagnosis, treatment planning, and prognosis
Combines heterogeneous LLM outputs by aligning and calibrating divergent reasoning
Evaluated against frontier models on the large RareBench dataset
evidence_signal: On RareBench (157,525 cases across all 33 Orphanet categories and 7,000+ conditions), RareLens outperformed GPT-5, DeepSeek-R1, Claude-3.7-Sonnet, and Gemini-2.5-Pro, with AUC 0.917 for screening and top-1 accuracies of 65.5% for diagnosis and 89.8% for treatment.
watch_item: Performance is reported on benchmark and external study data, so real-world impact, workflow fit, and safety across diverse clinical settings still need prospective validation.
paper_title: RareLens: Towards End-to-End Rare Disease Care via Aligning Divergent Large Language Model Reasoning
